review_notes: I read the whole file and the Cube/Walsh/ThreeBitTest definitions it depends on. I also searched Mathlib for the bijection-sum lemmas (Equiv.sum_comp, Fintype.sum_equiv). Most of the file is deliberately concrete: the clone-gap constants 48, 24, 64 and 6912, and the three-variable XOR equations. I did not flag these. The ℝ-valued coefficient lemmas depend on the ℝ-valued `coefficient`, so I left them alone. I did not compile the proposed statements. The universe finding assumes no downstream code relies on `Equation` living in `Type 0`, and I did not check every use in the repository. The same sum_cubeFlip/sum_cubeToggle lemmas are copied into several other files, so a general version would pay off more widely.

findings.excerpt:
theorem sum_cubeFlip (F : Cube I → ℝ) : (∑ f, F (cubeFlip f)) = ∑ f, F f := by
  refine Finset.sum_bij (fun f _ => cubeFlip f) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
findings.problem: The statement is an invariance of a finite sum under a bijection of the index set, but it is specialised to ℝ-valued F. The proof uses no property of ℝ beyond addition and commutativity, and it re-proves a bijection by hand with Finset.sum_bij. Any user who needs the same reindexing for ℕ-, ℂ- or vector-valued functions has to redo it.
findings.proposed_change: State it as `theorem sum_cubeFlip {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (F : Cube I → M) : (∑ f, F (cubeFlip f)) = ∑ f, F f`. Prove it from an involution-as-equivalence: `(Function.Involutive.toPerm cubeFlip (cubeFlip_cubeFlip)).sum_comp F`, which is Equiv.sum_comp applied to the equivalence given by the involution `cubeFlip` (this form is untested). Alternatively keep the existing Finset.sum_bij proof unchanged; it type-checks for any AddCommMonoid. The existing ℝ call in coefficient_zero_of_odd is an instance of the general statement.
findings.benefit: The lemma works for any additive commutative monoid, so downstream files can use it directly. The same copy-pasted lemma appears in several sibling Folding files. The proof also becomes shorter and does not repeat the bijection obligations.

findings.problem: This is the same bijection-invariance statement, specialised to ℝ-valued F although the proof only uses the fact that cubeToggle i is an involution. The two bijection-sum lemmas could be one general reindexing principle.
findings.proposed_change: State it as `theorem sum_cubeToggle {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (i : I) (F : Cube I → M) : (∑ f, F (cubeToggle i f)) = ∑ f, F f`. Prove it with `(Function.Involutive.toPerm (cubeToggle i) (cubeToggle_twice i)).sum_comp F`, or keep the existing Finset.sum_bij proof, which does not use ℝ. The use in conditioned_coefficient_zero_invalid is an ℝ instance, so it still elaborates.
findings.benefit: Users get a reusable reindexing lemma for any additive commutative monoid at no cost to the current ℝ call site. The proof can also be shortened by using Mathlib's Equiv.sum_comp.

findings.excerpt:
structure Equation (Name : Type) where
  first : Name
findings.problem: `Equation`, the variable `{Name : Type}`, `{I J : Type}` in FoldedEquation, `{I : Type}` in EmptyContext, and the `{Name Name' : Type}` binders in mapEquation, satisfied_mapEquation, satisfied_repeated_right and mapped_equationAcceptance_eq_half are all fixed at `Type`. The lemmas they depend on (Cube, walsh, coefficient, thirdQuery, and the first Hastad section's `{I : Type*}`) are universe-polymorphic. Nothing in the proofs uses the universe. Equation, satisfied, clone and the folded-equation lemmas therefore cannot be used with names or index types from a higher universe, even though the first Hastad section of this same file handles `Type*`.
findings.proposed_change: Change `structure Equation (Name : Type)` to `structure Equation (Name : Type*)`, and replace `{Name : Type}` (line 203), `{I J : Type}` (line 488), `{I : Type}` (line 680) and the `{Name Name' : Type}` binders (lines 549, 667, 674, 783) by `Type*`. The proofs are by rfl, cases or simp and do not depend on universes. Address uses HalfCube (a subtype) and Sum, which are universe-polymorphic. CloneGap's `Name × Index` with `Index = Nat` stays valid at `max u 0`.
findings.benefit: The equation and folding API works for arbitrary universe levels, consistent with the first section of the file and with the Walsh/ThreeBitTest dependencies. This avoids universe-lifting workarounds in downstream reductions that use larger types.
